summary: CNAME shadowing by corporate DNS forwarder causes SNI hostname mismatch and selective artifact 403s during shard fetch
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s when Redwood control plane attempts to download model shard presigned URLs during control-plane-initiated artifact fetches from S3. Failures are selective (only some shards fail), and occur only for the customer's private deployment behind a corporate DNS forwarder and egress proxy.

Impact:
- FinLedger sees ~10-20% of nightly shard fetches fail causing degraded cold-start time and occasional fallback to smaller model variants.
- Customer reports production inference errors during scale-up events.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) peered via TGW to corporate network
- Egress path: serving nodes -> VPC egress -> corporate DNS forwarder -> internet egress proxy -> AWS S3 (presigned URLs)
- Region: us-west-2, prod

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model scale-up on customer's private cluster (simulate a cache-miss by restarting a serving node).
2) Control plane issues presigned GETs to S3 for model shard objects from serving nodes.
3) Observe that 1 in 5 shard GETs return 403 from S3 while others succeed.
4) Re-query resolved A/AAAA and CNAME for the presigned host from inside the forwarding resolver and compare to direct public resolution.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- curl -v "<presigned-url-for-shard>" shows TLS handshake succeeded but HTTP 403.
- tcpdump on serving node shows SNI sent on ClientHello as host=presigned-<hash>.s3.amazonaws.com but resolved IPs are a mix of public S3 IPs and a privately-aliased front-end owned by the customer's corp-proxy.
- dig @corp-forwarder for presigned host returns a CNAME chain: presigned-<hash>.s3.amazonaws.com -> s3-redirect.internal-corp.example.com -> <corp-egress-ip>. The intermediate CNAME is only present when queried via corp resolver; public resolvers return canonical s3 endpoints.
- ALPN offered by corp-egress terminator is h2 but the TLS stack on the egress terminator strips or rewrites SNI in-flight for the proxied connection to the upstream S3 endpoint which leads to AWS treating the Host header as mismatched from the presigned URL hostname in the signed request (403).

Initial hypothesis:
- Corporate DNS forwarder is injecting an internal CNAME (shadowing) to steer traffic through an HTTP/TLS egress terminator. The presigned URLs are sensitive to exact hostnames used during the TLS handshake and request signature validation; the egress terminator rewrites SNI or host headers which invalidates the presigned signature on some call paths, producing intermittent 403s. The mix of responses is due to resolver cache eviction / round-robin between internal-corp alias and direct IPs.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC - Aisha Patel: Customer provided failing curl output and tcpdump. Observed mixed IPs and CNAME only when querying corp resolver.
2026-03-13 11:03 UTC - Marcus Chen: Reproduced in our staging replicate using a corporate-forwarder VM emulation; confirmed intermediate CNAME insertion and SNI rewriting on egress appliance.

2026-03-13 12:20 UTC - Marcus Chen: Compared request signature string used in presigned GETs; when SNI/Host differs from presigned hostname, AWS returns 403 as expected. Documented exact header mismatch waterfall.
2026-03-13 14:45 UTC - Support: Noted correlation between TTLs of internal-corp CNAME and observed failure rate — when TTL expires, resolver falls back to public resolution and requests succeed.
2026-03-13 16:10 UTC - Support/SRE: Confirmed that some corp egress nodes rewrite SNI to canonicalize hostnames for TLS inspection. This breaks presigned URL validation.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13 09:30 UTC: Looping in FinLedger network/security team. Asked for corp-forwarder config and appliance vendor logs. Provided packet captures and failing curl output.

FinLedger (Customer) 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC: We see proxy-side TLS inspection, but believed it only terminated on outbound web traffic; attaching proxy logs that show rewrite actions. We cannot change proxy behavior without risk approvals.

Marcus Chen (SRE) 2026-03-13 11:15 UTC: Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) pin control-plane artifact-relay to use our internal artifact-relay gateway (tunneled via Redwood control plane) or 2) configure the customer's egress to allow direct passthrough for s3.amazonaws.com hostnames to preserve original SNI/Host. Asked for timeline for corporate change.
FinLedger Network Team 2026-03-13 13:30 UTC: Can whitelist s3.amazonaws.com but their corporate policy prevents passthrough by default; need exception ticket and 48-hour change window.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: enabled control-plane artifact-relay for FinLedger so shard downloads are proxied via Redwood-managed egress (preserving presigned hostname and avoiding corp SNI rewrite). Customer confirmed shard fetch success rate returned to 100% after switch.
Permanent next steps: 1) Customer to submit change request to allow SNI passthrough for s3.amazonaws.com or to stop the proxy from rewriting SNI for presigned hostnames. 2) Engineering follow-up: add detection/alerting when presigned-hostname resolution returns CNAMEs to non-AWS domains and auto-failover to artifact-relay for private deployments.
Post-incident tasks: create runbook entry for "CNAME shadowing / SNI rewrite causing presigned URL 403s" and expose a diagnostic script to customers to detect CNAME shadowing.
postmortem_followup: Add runbook and alerting: detect CNAMEs that do not end in aws domain when resolving presigned hosts (ENG-PR-901)
Add UI note in Console for private deployments: warning when custom DNS resolves presigned hostnames to non-AWS CNAMEs (DOCS-412)
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to provide template customer firewall/DNS exceptions for presigned artifact fetches
